one_sentence_story: With a cotton swab and a $10 mirror propped inside a cardboard box, V. S. Ramachandran showed that missing limbs stay alive on the brain's body map — and that tricking visual cortex into seeing a healthy reflected hand open can unclench years of frozen phantom cramping.
so_what_for_you: Never underestimate multisensory feedback: in rehabilitation and motor recovery, giving your brain clean visual proof of smooth, safe movement helps calm protective motor guarding.

jargon_map.plain: vivid sensation that an amputated arm or leg is still present, moving, or cramping
jargon_map.analogy: like a unplugged telephone extension whose office number still lights up on the central switchboard

jargon_map.plain: neighboring sensory zones (like the face) expanding responsiveness into adjacent silent territory (like the missing hand) on the somatosensory strip
jargon_map.analogy: like next-door neighbors annexing an empty apartment

jargon_map.plain: motor cortex sending 'open hand!' commands while zero visual or joint feedback returns, locking in 'learned paralysis'
